cases.title: Escape must return focus to the button that opened the dialog
cases.summary: With opacity-based hiding, closing the dialog pulls focus back into the invisible dialog instead of the opener.

cases.title: Escape in a nested menubar submenu must close only that submenu and return focus to its parent item
cases.summary: Pressing Escape inside a second-level submenu collapses every open submenu and throws focus back to the top-level menubar item.

cases.title: An open disclosure-navigation dropdown must close when keyboard focus moves out of the navigation
cases.summary: After opening the Shop dropdown and tabbing on to the page's search field, the dropdown stays open over the content.

cases.title: The combobox's aria-activedescendant must reference the highlighted suggestion element
cases.summary: Arrowing through suggestions sets aria-activedescendant to the suggestion's text instead of its element id, so screen readers cannot announce the highlighted option.

cases.title: Enter must choose the suggestion that is highlighted after the search is refined
cases.summary: After navigating suggestions and then typing more, Enter selects a different suggestion from the one shown as highlighted.

cases.title: One Tab press must move from an autocomplete field with open suggestions to the next form field
cases.summary: With suggestions open, Tab sends focus into the suggestion list instead of the next field, so keyboard users must press Tab twice.

cases.title: Escape on a closed dropdown toggle inside a modal must close the modal
cases.summary: When focus is on a closed dropdown button inside a modal, the dropdown swallows the Escape key, so keyboard users cannot dismiss the modal.

cases.title: Shift+Tab from the first control in a modal must wrap to the modal's last control
cases.summary: Pressing Shift+Tab on the first control of an open modal throws focus back to the modal container instead of wrapping to the last control, so keyboard users can never move backwards through the dialog.

cases.title: A non-modal offcanvas panel that allows page scrolling must not trap keyboard focus
cases.summary: With body scrolling enabled and no backdrop, every attempt to Tab to a page control behind the open offcanvas pulls focus back into the panel, so keyboard users cannot use the page while the panel is open.

cases.title: Escape must close the dropdown menu and return focus to its toggle button
cases.summary: After arrowing into a dropdown menu, pressing Escape hides the menu but leaves keyboard focus on the hidden item instead of the toggle button.

cases.title: An offcanvas panel opened with a backdrop must keep keyboard focus inside the panel
cases.summary: With body scrolling and a backdrop both enabled, opening the offcanvas leaves focus on the page behind the backdrop, so Tab moves through obscured page controls instead of the panel.

cases.title: Arrow keys in a tab list must move keyboard focus to the newly selected tab
cases.summary: Pressing ArrowRight selects the next tab and shows its panel, but focus stays on the previous tab, so the next arrow press re-selects the same tab and keyboard users cannot walk the tab list.

cases.title: Arrow keys in a tab list must skip disabled tabs
cases.summary: Pressing ArrowRight from the active tab selects the next tab even though it is disabled, showing its panel and leaving focus on a tab that is no longer selected.

cases.title: When a list row containing the focused button is removed inside a focus trap, focus must stay inside the trap
cases.summary: Pressing Remove on a basket row deletes the row and drops keyboard focus to the page body behind the open dialog.

cases.title: When the focused control inside a focus trap removes itself, focus must stay inside the trap
cases.summary: Pressing a Show all button that removes itself drops keyboard focus to the page body behind the open dialog.

cases.title: Typing past a character limit must keep the text and say how many characters are too many
cases.summary: The character count leaves the textarea's hard maxlength in place, so typing is silently cut off at the limit and the user is never told the text is too long.

cases.title: Header navigation links that are visible on a desktop-width page must not be hidden from screen readers
cases.summary: On wide screens the header script marks the always-visible navigation aria-hidden, so screen reader users cannot find the links that keyboard focus still lands on.

cases.title: Moving to a radio in another group with the same name must hide the conditional question that no longer applies
cases.summary: When one radio question is built from two radios groups, choosing the opt-out answer leaves the previous answer's mobile number field on screen even though that answer is no longer selected.

cases.title: The up and down arrow keys must not switch between horizontal tabs
cases.summary: Pressing the down arrow on a tab to move on through the page instead switches to the next tab, which a reported NVDA user experienced as being trapped in the tab list.

cases.title: Activating a form control inside a modal must not close the modal
cases.summary: Pressing Space on a checkbox inside the modal closes the modal and leaves the checkbox unticked, because the overlay close trigger matches every click inside it.

cases.title: Tabbing past the last visible control of a modal must wrap inside the modal even when it contains hidden buttons
cases.summary: A modal with a display:none Try again button lets Tab escape from the last visible control to the page behind the modal.

cases.title: Ticking a 'None of these' checkbox must clear the other answers in its group even when each checkbox has its own name
cases.summary: When symptoms are posted as separately named fields in one exclusive group, ticking 'No, I do not have any of these symptoms' leaves the earlier symptoms ticked, so contradictory answers are submitted.

cases.title: ArrowLeft must keep moving the caret in other text fields while a calendar is shown
cases.summary: With a calendar visible, pressing ArrowLeft in any other text field is swallowed, so the user cannot move the caret back to correct their text.

cases.title: Form fields inside a disabled fieldset must not be treated as tabbable, so a focus-trapped dialog focuses its first usable field
cases.summary: Opening the delivery address dialog leaves keyboard focus behind on the page, because the trap tries to focus a select inside a disabled fieldset.

cases.title: Tabbing out of a date field with an out-of-range date must close the calendar
cases.summary: If the date field holds a date outside the allowed range, tabbing away leaves the calendar popup open over the form.

cases.title: Pressing Tab in an open date field must move focus to the next form field
cases.summary: Tabbing out of the date field sends focus into the closing calendar's hidden buttons, so focus is lost instead of reaching the next field.

benchmark.note: Each frozen implementation is scored on its own: the first auto run per screened case on that version is the score. From engine v9, every case gets three blind runs and every run counts; none is picked. Changing the engine or a run limit starts a new version; every case is rerun and earlier scores stay listed.

versions.note: First frozen engine, run while the case set was still being built. No indentation-insensitive patch matching.
Adds indentation-insensitive patch matching. Output limit 12,000 tokens, prompt limit 96,000 characters: three Ultra replies were cut off before the patch and one case was never sent.

Output limit 32,000 tokens, prompt limit 240,000 characters, five-minute call timeout. All 26 cases rerun. Later review: one of its 20 passes (bootstrap-modal-shift-tab-wrap) hardcoded the test page's #confirm-close and #confirm-delete into modal.js; version 6 rejects such patches.

When a patch does not apply, the model is told which of its lines are not in the file and the closest real line, or where an ambiguous match occurs, instead of a one-line error. Same limits. All 26 cases rerun.

Adds an overfitting gate: a patch that makes component code name one of the test page's element ids is rejected and sent back (it caught two earlier passes that hardcoded the page). The browser now records, for each key, whether it was cancelled and whether a dialog's cancel event could be cancelled, and the model sees that trace. All 26 cases and all open bugs rerun.

When a patch does not apply, the retry gets the file lines it was aimed at and the first line that differs; a path naming only the tail of one allowed file is resolved. Scored 18/26, below v6: most misses were patches that did not apply because the model misremembered an unchanged line (a dropped semicolon, self for this) or copied lines from its own rejected patch. That led to version 8. All 26 cases and all open bugs rerun.

An unchanged line the model misremembered (spacing, a trailing semicolon, self for this) is replaced by the file's own line; changed lines may differ only in formatting and no line may be inserted. Advisory fields nested inside an edit are moved back to the plan, and after an unapplied patch the model is told nothing was applied. Verification is unchanged. All 26 cases and all open bugs rerun.

A patch whose before misremembers, invents or omits context lines is applied hunk by hunk to the real region when the lines it deletes exist verbatim and contiguously, the region is unique and every insertion has a defined place; the ignored context is recorded. An axe finding counts as new only if no recorded path on the original (keyboard, pointer, guards) showed the same rule on the same kind of element. Committed on 2026-10-26 after the first 4 of its runs: every case gets three blind runs on this engine and every run counts; the first run is the score comparable with earlier versions.

Engine v10, stopped after 2 of its planned 78 runs. It asked Nemotron 3 for schema-constrained JSON (response_format). The replies parsed, but code inside the strings came back corrupted (newlines as a bare n or dropped, quotes as guillemets), so all six patches failed to apply. Both runs stay recorded; they are not a fair score of the other changes, which carry on in v11.

Engine v11: v10 without response_format. The page around the library is read-only context: the model sees it without a hash, and an edit to it is refused with the list of component files, so a pass has to change the library (35 of 193 earlier passing runs only worked around the bug in the page). A reply that does not parse has only its bracket structure repaired (18 of 30 recorded Super failures recover). Committed on 2026-10-26 before any run: three blind runs per bug, every run counted; the first run is the score comparable with earlier versions.

Engine v12: library files are no longer hidden from repairs. A prefix match on package, lock and config had excluded everything under packages/ (GOV.UK tabs, NHS.UK checkboxes) and util/config.js or configure.js; only build-tool configs (*.config.js) are now excluded by name. A path written with a leading ./ resolves, and a mistyped sha256 that matches no file is recorded instead of rejecting the edit. Committed on 2026-10-26 before any run: three blind runs per bug, every run counted; the first run is the score comparable with earlier versions.

Engine v13: up to five proposals instead of three. Nemotron 3 Super makes the first; Nemotron 3 Ultra makes up to four retries, each given Chromium's failure report. The local page server also picks another port when the OS hands out one that Chromium refuses (one v12 run was lost to port 5061). GitHub Actions live runs keep three proposals. Committed on 2026-10-26 before any run: three blind runs per bug, every run counted; the first run is the score comparable with earlier versions.
